doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Coltrane as spiritual hero, and discovering Charlie Parker
summary: Levy describes his devotion to Coltrane and his quartet, other early albums, and first hearing Charlie Parker on Massey Hall.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: If you started with “Crescent” and Roland Kirk and so forth, did your tastes or listening habits go backwards?

Yeah. I started listening, you know I listened a lot to that radio station and of course Coltrane, as many other people were, I was fixated on Coltrane. I mean it was like a religion for me. And for many others as well. It doesn’t matter like what country you’re from, if you’re white or black or Muslim, Christian, Jewish, it doesn’t matter. He had a transcendent message that he was broadcasting through his music that affected many people in this deeply spiritual and religious way. I mean I compare him to Bach. I really

do. Because he was so mathematical at the same time as he was so spiritual. And the supporting cast was ridiculous, I mean McCoy and Jimmy Garrison and Elvin. I mean this is something that doesn’t happen too often in the history of music where you get four individuals with such amazing individual contributions and that are all playing together as one mind. And so this was overwhelming for me. But then I did of course get into all sorts of other people. I remember the Sonny Rollins “Live at the Village Vanguard” was one of the other albums I listened to a lot, and all the Jazz Messengers albums and then I went back and heard Bird. I remember one night I’m listening, I’m in bed listening to my radio, you know my parents think I’m asleep and I’m listening to the jazz station. And they played the “Live at Massey Hall” album. And I just about fell out of bed. That was the first time I heard Bird. And I said, “This is how – he plays the way I feel when I play is how this guy plays.” It’s like wow. So Charlie Parker, still, there’s nobody that sounds like Bird.
